principle: TTF learns from training species without seeing the named boundary. External biogeographic boundary geometry is frozen prospectively and used only after held-out transfer scoring.
admissibility: important biogeographic boundary defined independently of the focal trait
multiple replicate species or systems when used for a cross-species TTF claim
georeferenced observations spanning the relevant spatial domain
trait measurement not selected or tuned using TTF response
species inclusion frozen before TTF outcomes are inspected
external boundary geometry frozen before final scoring
primary TTF field is fit blind to the named boundary
pairwise genetic distance matrix cells are never shuffled

benchmarks.boundary_system: Iranian Plateau mountain areas of endemism
benchmarks.trait_domain: population genetic distance from RADseq SNPs
benchmarks.sampling: 8-15 localities per species across at least 3 mountain regions
benchmarks.input_plan: population coordinates from Table S1; SNP data from Appendix S1/S2; prospectively compute population-level Nei and Rogers distances
benchmarks.ttf_plan: fit species-disjoint TTF to genetic-distance turnover without boundary labels; test transfer first; compare learned transition support to frozen biogeographic breaks second
benchmarks.attribution_caveat: raw genetic distance can contain isolation by distance; boundary attribution requires a separately qualified cross-fitted distance nuisance or paired D/G predictor comparison
